chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id narrated from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa, from Ibn Miskan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abi ‘Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

The nafilah prayer is eight rak‘ahs when the sun declines before al-zuhr, and six rak‘ahs after al-zuhr, and two rak‘ahs before al-‘asr, and four rak‘ahs after al-maghrib, and two rak‘ahs after al-‘isha’ al-akhirah in which you recite one hundred verses, standing or sitting, though standing is better; and do not count these two among the fifty. And eight rak‘ahs are in the latter part of the night; in salat al-layl you recite:
in the first two rak‘ahs, and in the remainder of it you recite whatever of the Qur’an you wish. Then al-watr is three rak‘ahs; in all of them you recite:
and you separate between them with taslim. Then the two rak‘ahs that are before al-fajr: in the first of them you recite:

As for the hadiths which have been narrated regarding a lesser number than what we have mentioned of the prayer, such as what was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Bint Ilyas, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Aba ‘Abd Allah عليه السلام saying: “Do not pray less than forty-four rak‘ahs.” He said: And I saw him praying four rak‘ahs after al-‘atamah. There is no prohibition in this report against what exceeds forty-four; rather, he عليه السلام only prohibited reducing it below that. And it is not impossible that he عليه السلام encouraged these forty-four rak‘ahs because of their emphasis and the strength of their recommendation by this report, while encouraging what is besides them by another hadith. We have already presented hadiths that include that.

And as for what was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Yahya ibn Habib, who said: I asked al-Rida عليه السلام about the most excellent thing by which the servants draw near to Allah, the Exalted, from prayer. He said: “Forty-six rak‘ahs, its obligatory acts and its nawafil.” I said: This is the narration of Zurarah. He said: “Do you see anyone who was more outspoken with the truth than him?” This hadith also contains no prohibition regarding prayers besides these; rather, he was asked about the most excellent means by which the servants draw near, so he mentioned these forty-six and singled them out because what exceeds them in prayers is below them in merit. This indicates that the intended meaning is what we have mentioned, and that he intended to emphasize the merit of these forty-six rak‘ahs.

key_terms.الْعِشَاءِ الْآخِرَةِ: the night obligatory prayer, after which a recommended two-rak‘ah prayer is performed
key_terms.الْوَتْرُ: the concluding set of night prayer rak‘ahs mentioned here as three separated by taslim
key_terms.تَسْلِيمٍ: the salutation that marks the completion of a prayer unit or set
key_terms.صَلَاةُ النَّافِلَةِ: the supererogatory prayer performed in addition to the obligatory salat
key_terms.صَلَاةِ اللَّيْلِ: the night prayer performed in the latter part of the night

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended daily nawafil rak‘ahs and recitations according to Imam al-Sadiq and Imam al-Rida عليهما السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith outlines the structure and timing of the daily nawafil, including the night prayer, al-watr, and the two rak‘ahs before al-fajr, along with recommended Qur’anic recitations in some of them. It also cites related reports and explains that narrations mentioning forty-four or forty-six rak‘ahs indicate emphasized and especially meritorious prayers, not a prohibition against additional recommended prayers.
